name: Lake Besh-Tash
near: Beshtash — ~6.3 km as the crow flies (OSM marker, catalog calculation; in reality a small settlement/ranger post in the gorge). Kozhuchak is the village at the entrance to the gorge; the town of Talas is 47 km to the north (too.kg).
elev: About 3000 m (too.kg, nomad.kg, map.kg); central-asia.guide — 2997 m. The start of the walking section in the TUK program is 2675 m.
short: A turquoise high-mountain lake (~3000 m, 28 m deep) at the end of the 30 km Besh-Tash gorge — the main goal of the nature park of the same name, 47 km south of Talas.
desc: Besh-Tash is the largest of the eight mountain lakes of the Besh-Tash nature park in the Talas Ala-Too (too.kg). The lake lies at an elevation of about 3000 m, is 28 m deep and covers about 0.5 km² (central-asia.guide; too.kg); the water is turquoise, and there is a small unnamed lake below the main one (too.kg). Trout, marinka (snowtrout) and osman (Tien Shan scaly osman) live in the lake and river (map.kg, 2024). The name “Besh-Tash” means “five stones”: in the gorge stand five stones tied to a legend about robbers (too.kg). The road runs along the Besh-Tash River almost up to the moraine below the lake; per too.kg it is a 15-minute walk from the end of the road to the water, but per nomad.kg an ordinary car only reaches the park checkpoint, and the last 20–25 km are on foot or by 4×4 / SUV.
guide: Besh-Tash is a rare case where you can see a 3,000-metre lake without a multi-day trek: by 4×4 / SUV through the gorge almost to the moraine, and then 15 minutes on foot to the turquoise water. If you are in an ordinary car, leave it at the park checkpoint and allow a day for the 20–25 km through the gorge — or camp in a tent by the lake, there are plenty of campsites. Along the way look out for those very “five stones” that gave the gorge its name. There is no mobile signal; drink water from the lake and river only after boiling. The best time is July — August, when it is warm and yurts stand in the gorge.
see: Turquoise Lake Besh-Tash and the small lake below; the moraine below the lake; the Besh-Tash gorge with juniper, spruce and Semenov fir; the “five stones” that gave the gorge its name; flowering meadows in May — June (too.kg; nomad.kg).
skip: You have an ordinary passenger car and no spare day for a 20–25 km walk from the checkpoint. You are not ready for a night at 3000 m without a signal or infrastructure. You want a “lake with services” — there is no cafe or lodging here.
diff: Easy with a 4×4 / SUV (15 min on foot from the moraine — too.kg); moderate on foot from the checkpoint (20–25 km one way through the gorge — nomad.kg) or in the TUK program (start 2675 m, ~325 m of climbing to 3000 m). Altitude 3000 m.
when: July — August: passes are open, it is warm, yurt camps operate (nomad.kg); May — June — tulips and blooms (but ice and snow may lie by the lake); September — golden autumn. too.kg advises April — May to catch the ice melt — at 3000 m the approach may be blocked by snow at that time (not confirmed). In winter access is limited.
hours: Through the checkpoint of the Besh-Tash nature park with payment of a fee; the checkpoint's opening hours are not published.
daytime: Morning — smooth water and a rich turquoise colour before clouds and wind (editorial).
how: From Talas south ~13 km to the entrance of the Besh-Tash gorge (central-asia.guide), then along a dirt road beside the river: an ordinary car goes as far as the park checkpoint, the remaining 20–25 km are on foot or by 4×4 / SUV (nomad.kg); too.kg writes that a good dirt road reaches almost to the lake, with a 15-minute walk from the moraine. About 47 km in total from Talas. From Bishkek to Talas — 5.5–8 h (marshrutka (minibus)/taxi via Otmok or GoBus via Kazakhstan).
needcar: Yes: a taxi/your own car from Talas; to get close to the lake — a 4×4 / SUV (otherwise on foot from the checkpoint).
self: Yes: no border permit is needed, just pay the park fee at the checkpoint. Without a 4×4 / SUV — a long walk in; there is no signal — tell someone your route.
roadtype: A dirt road through the gorge along the Besh-Tash River; to the checkpoint — passable for passenger cars, beyond that a 4×4 / SUV (nomad.kg); too.kg describes the road as a good dirt road almost to the lake. From the moraine — a 15 min trail.
traveltime: Talas — park checkpoint ~30–40 min (estimate); checkpoint — lake: 20–25 km, ~1.5–2 h by 4×4 / SUV or 6–8 h on foot one way (estimate based on nomad.kg); from the moraine — 15 min on foot (too.kg). From Bishkek to the park — about 4–5 h by car (map.kg says “about 4 hours”).
stay: By the lake — tents only, with plenty of campsites (too.kg); the park has equipped camping zones at various elevations, campfires are allowed (map.kg, 2024); in summer yurt camps operate in the gorge (nomad.kg; names and prices not found). Guesthouses are in Talas ($10–30) and through CBT Talas.
net: There is no mobile signal at the lake (too.kg; visitsilkroad.org).
entry: Besh-Tash nature park fee: 250 som per person and 400 som per vehicle (nomad.kg; publication year not given). The official Forest Service price list was not found.
transfer: Not confirmed: prices for a 4×4 / SUV or taxi Talas — lake are not published. To Talas: GoBus 500 som (2025), marshrutka (minibus) ~350 som, shared taxi from ~650 som.
bring: A tent and a warm sleeping bag (a night at 3000 m), a down jacket, a rain jacket, a stove and means of boiling/purifying water (drink water from the lake and river only after boiling — visitsilkroad.org), food for the whole trip, cash for the park fee (250 + 400 som), sun protection.
warn: No mobile signal. At 3000 m altitude sickness is possible, and nights are cold even in summer. Boil water. Brown bears live in the park (central-asia.guide) — store food properly. Do not drink or wash with soap in the lake. In a passenger car you can only get as far as the checkpoint; in bad weather the dirt road gets washed out.
food: At the gorge's yurt camps in summer — kumis and shepherds' home food (not confirmed for specific places); in Talas — dishes with Talas beans.
reviews: Google Maps: 5.0 from 10 ratings (catalog check, 10.2026). No reviews with a meaningful sample were found on TripAdvisor or 2GIS; descriptions note the turquoise colour of the water and easy access by 4×4 / SUV.
p.sum: Lake Besh-Tash (~3000 m) is a 1–2 day objective from Talas: 13 km of paved road to the gorge entrance at Kozhuchak, payment at the park's automatic checkpoint (since 28.07.2026, by card/QR), then a dirt road — a passenger car as far as the checkpoint, a 4×4 / SUV higher up to the camp meadows (~2675 m); from there 6 km on foot (12 km round trip, +325 m). The most convenient is a 4×4 / SUV from Talas or a Trekking Union group trip (5500 som). Camp in a tent in the park or stay in Talas.

p.permits: No border permit needed. Besh-Tash National Park fee: 250 som/person and 400 som/vehicle (nomad.kg, year not stated); since 28.07.2026 an automated checkpoint — payment by card, by QR or through an e-wallet. For reference: general nature park tariffs in Kyrgyzstan in 2025 — 150–700 som depending on category (Kyrgyz/CIS/foreigners).
p.access: Children with hiking experience — yes (12 km, +325 m from the camp). Older people — only if driven up by 4×4 and at a slow pace. Wheelchair users — no. With a dog — possible, but the park has bears and shepherd dogs.
